t: Section 1833(g)(5) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395l(g)(5)) is amended by striking “2006” and inserting “the period beginning on January 1, 2006, and ending on December 31, 2007,”.

fable.w: This section only changes a date range in an existing Social Security Act provision, extending the period it covers. A tempting reading is that the underlying provision (the Medicare therapy cap exceptions process) lets outside parties request something from the government, but the amendment itself creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue. Requests for an exception would in any case resemble applications for benefits, which are not participation.
fable.s: is amended by striking “2006” and inserting “the period beginning on January 1, 2006, and ending on December 31, 2007,”

opus.w: This amendment only changes the period a Social Security Act provision covers, from 2006 to 2006–2007. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties or right to sue. The underlying therapy-cap exceptions process involves requests for benefits, which the definition does not count as participation.
opus.s: is amended by striking “2006” and inserting “the period beginning on January 1, 2006, and ending on December 31, 2007,”
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Section 1833(g)(5) sets up the Medicare therapy-cap exceptions process, which suggests beneficiaries or providers ask the government for something. That fails. This amendment only changes a date, and an exceptions request would be an application for benefits anyway, which the definition excludes.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a direct statutory amendment changing a specific date range. It does not create any mechanism for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The decision is made by Congress through the text of the law itself, without requiring input from entities outside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: Section 1833(g)(5) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395l(g)(5)) is amended by striking “2006” and inserting “the period beginning on January 1, 2006, and ending on December 31, 2007,”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the date range for a program could implicitly involve public comment or consultation if the program itself is participatory. However, this specific text is merely a technical amendment to a date in the statute. It does not establish any process for outside parties to consult, comment, or participate in the decision to change the date. The change is made by Congress directly through the amendment.
